Introduction

The Nabu compiler is a polyglot compiler that compiles source code into Java bytecode so it can be executed on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).

Writing a compiler is a complex task that takes a lot of time and usually requires a lot of expertise about the JVM. The goal of the Nabu compiler is to make this easier: it is designed to be extendable, so you can add support for your own language without having to write a compiler from scratch.

What can you do with Nabu?

  • Compile the Nabu language to JVM bytecode. Nabu is a programming language whose syntax is based on Java and Kotlin.
  • Interoperate with Java. Nabu and Java code can be mixed in a single project, and Nabu code can call Java code and vice versa. Java 20 is supported.
  • Write DSLs. The compiler supports domain-specific languages (DSLs) so you can write code that is more readable and maintainable for a specific domain. See DSL support for an example with JPA.
  • Target multiple backends. Beyond the standard ASM backend (JVM bytecode), experimental backends exist for the JDK ClassFile API and LLVM (native).
  • Add your own language. The compiler is extended via plugins. Provide a language parser that parses source code and builds an AST, and the compiler does the rest.
Extendable by design. The compiler defines extension points. Just provide a language parser, an element resolver, or a code transformer, and register it in a `plugin.xml` file.

The simplest extension

Because the compiler is built around plugins, adding a language is largely about providing a LanguageParser:

public class SimpleLanguageParser implements LanguageParser {

    private final FileObject.Kind SOURCE_KIND = new FileObject.Kind(".simple", true);

    @Override
    public FileObject.Kind getSourceKind() {
        return SOURCE_KIND;
    }

    @Override
    public CompilationUnit parse(final FileObject fileObject,
                                 final CompilerContext compilerContext) {
        // TODO: Implement parsing logic for .simple files
        return null;
    }
}

Demo application

A demo application is available at the Nabu petstore repository, showing the compiler in action.

Getting started

To use Nabu and Java together in a Maven project, see the Maven Plugin documentation. For IDE support, check out the Nabu Idea plugin for IntelliJ.
